name: 41 - The Bone Minuet: A Death Cleric's Flute

pages.name: An unsettling encounter, not an automatic fight

text.content:
STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

The Bone Minuet

Optional, 10-15 minutes. Place at the graveyard or between dream rooms. The flute-player may be a visiting death cleric named Veyra, or a PC death cleric when this is their scene. The original request did not require the cleric to be evil.

The first notes are almost too soft to separate from the wind. Then the rhythm settles, and pale shapes begin to move among the gravestones.

Skeletons turn in measured pairs. A rusted breastplate dips in a courtly bow. A scrap of funeral silk circles an empty ribcage. Their feet touch the earth lightly, as if remembering the dance matters more than holding their weight.

At the centre stands a death cleric in dark travelling robes, playing a bone flute. The music is mournful, not frantic. Each time a note falters, one dancer hesitates.

The cleric lowers the instrument. Every skull turns toward you.

'There is room,' the cleric says. 'The living may join.'

What is happening

Veyra is preserving a funeral dance whose participants' names were erased. The skeletons are not the five freshly murdered witnesses and are not proof all undead serve the hags. The dance offers a way to honour the forgotten without restoring them to life.

Choices

Join respectfully, offer a remembered name, or ask about the tune. A specific gesture of respect succeeds without a roll. DC 14 Performance or Religion can earn a further detail: the flute's rhythm leaves deliberate gaps where the coven's song demands continuous repetition.

Reward: one remembrance anchor or a Lucid token. Veyra says, 'Leave space between the notes. That is where another voice can answer.' This supports the organ solution without replacing it.

If attacked: the dancers defend and disengage; use owned skeleton statistics if needed. Do not turn a short atmospheric scene into dozens of initiative entries. Veyra ends the animation rather than sacrificing the dead to prolong combat.

The flute itself is a ritual prop, not an unlisted magic item with an automatic anti-hydra effect.
